api_token.description: API token with GraphQL access and `write_pipelines`, `read_pipelines` and `write_suites` REST API scopes. You can generate a token from [your settings page](https://buildkite.com/user/api-access-tokens/new?description=terraform&scopes[]=write_pipelines&scopes[]=write_suites&scopes[]=read_pipelines&scopes[]=graphql). If not provided, the value is taken from the `BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN` environment variable.

archive_pipeline_on_delete.description: Enable this to archive pipelines when destroying the resource. This is opposed to completely deleting pipelines.

graphql_url.description: Base URL for the GraphQL API to use. If not provided, the value is taken from the `BUILDKITE_GRAPHQL_URL` environment variable.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retry attempts for retryable HTTP requests. Defaults to 10.

organization.description: The Buildkite organization slug. This can be found on the [settings](https://buildkite.com/organizations/~/settings) page. If not provided, the value is taken from the `BUILDKITE_ORGANIZATION_SLUG` environment variable.

rest_url.description: Base URL for the REST API to use. If not provided, the value is taken from the `BUILDKITE_REST_URL` environment variable.

create.description: A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

delete.description: A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

read.description: A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.

update.description: A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

block.description: This provider can be used to manage resources on [buildkite.com](https://buildkite.com).

description.description: The description of the agent token. Used to help identify its use.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the agent token.

token.description: The token value used by an agent to register with the API.

uuid.description: The UUID of the agent token.

block.description:
This resource allows you to create and manage non-clustered agent tokens.
You can find out more about clusters in the Buildkite [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/v3/tokens).

color.description: A color representation of the Cluster. Accepts hex codes, eg #BADA55.

description.description:
This is a description for the cluster, this may describe the usage for it, the region, or something else
which would help identify the Cluster's purpose.

emoji.description:
An emoji to use with the Cluster, this can either be set using :buildkite: notation, or with the
emoji itself, such as 🚀.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster.

name.description: The name of the Cluster. Can only contain numbers and letters, no spaces or special characters.

block.description:
This resource allows you to create and manage a Buildkite Cluster to run your builds in.
Clusters are useful for grouping agents by there capabilities or permissions.
Find out more information in our [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/clusters/overview).

allowed_ip_addresses.description: A list of CIDR-notation IPv4 addresses from which agents can use this Cluster Agent Token.If not set, all IP addresses are allowed (the same as setting 0.0.0.0/0).

cluster_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the Cluster that this Cluster Agent Token belongs to.

cluster_uuid.description: The UUID of the Cluster that this token belongs to.

description.description: A description about what this cluster agent token is used for.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the token.

token.description: The token value used by an agent to register with the API.

block.description: A Cluster Agent Token is a token used to connect an agent to a cluster in Buildkite.

cluster_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster to which to add a default queue.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster.

key.description: The Key for the cluster queue; its unique identifier

queue_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster queue to set as default on the cluster.

block.description:
This resource allows you to manage a default queue for a Buildkite Cluster.
Find out more information in our [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/clusters/overview).

actor_email.description: The email of the actor (only for users).

actor_slug.description: The slug of the actor (only for teams).

actor_type.description: The type of the actor (user or team).

actor_uuid.description: The UUID of the actor (user or team) that is the maintainer.

id.description: The permission ID of the cluster maintainer.

team_uuid.description:
The UUID of the team to add as a maintainer. This is mutually exclusive with user_uuid.
Only one of user_uuid or team_uuid can be specified.

user_uuid.description:
The UUID of the user to add as a maintainer. This is mutually exclusive with team_uuid.
Only one of user_uuid or team_uuid can be specified.

block.description:
This resource allows you to manage cluster maintainers in Buildkite. Maintainers can be either users or teams
that have permission to manage a specific cluster. Find out more information in our
[documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/clusters/manage-clusters).

cluster_id.description: The ID of the cluster that this cluster queue belongs to.

cluster_uuid.description: The UUID of the cluster this queue belongs to.

description.description: A description for the cluster queue.

dispatch_paused.description: The dispatch state of a cluster queue.

instance_shape.description:
The instance shape to use for the Hosted Agent cluster queue. This can be a MacOS instance shape or a Linux instance shape.
Valid values are:
- MACOS_ARM64_M4_6X28
- MACOS_ARM64_M4_12X56
- LINUX_AMD64_2X4
- LINUX_AMD64_4X16
- LINUX_AMD64_8X32
- LINUX_AMD64_16X64
- LINUX_ARM64_2X4
- LINUX_ARM64_4X16
- LINUX_ARM64_8X32
- LINUX_ARM64_16X64

agent_image_ref.description: A URL reference to a container image that will be used for jobs running within the queue. This URL is required to be publicly available, or pushed to the internal registry available within the cluster. Please note that this value is currently experimental and in preview. Please contact support@buildkite.com to enable this functionality for your organization.

macos_version.description: Optional selection of a specific macOS version to be selected for jobs in the queue to have available. Please note that this value is currently experimental and may not function as expected.

xcode_version.description: Required selection of a specific XCode version to be selected for jobs in the queue to have available. Please note that this value is currently experimental and may not function as expected.

hosted_agents.description: Control the settings for the Buildkite hosted agents.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster queue.

key.description: The key of the cluster queue.

retry_agent_affinity.description: Specifies which agent should be preferred when a job is retried. Valid values are `prefer-warmest` (prefer agents that have recently finished jobs) and `prefer-different` (prefer a different agent if available). Defaults to `prefer-warmest`.

uuid.description: The UUID of the cluster queue.

block.description: A Cluster Queue is a queue belonging to a specific Cluster for its Agents to target builds on.

cluster_id.description: The UUID of the cluster this secret belongs to.

created_at.description: The time when the secret was created.

description.description: A description of what this secret is for.

id.description: The UUID of the cluster secret.

key.description: The key name for the secret. Must start with a letter and only contain letters, numbers, and underscores. Maximum 255 characters. Must not start with `buildkite` or `bk` (case-insensitive) as these prefixes are reserved.

policy.description: YAML access policy defining which pipelines and branches can access this secret.

updated_at.description: The time when the secret was last updated.

value.description: The secret value. Must be less than 8KB. Exactly one of `value` or `value_wo` must be configured. This value is stored in Terraform state; use `value_wo` with `value_wo_version` to avoid storing secret values in state.

value_wo.description: Write-only secret value. Must be less than 8KB. Exactly one of `value` or `value_wo` must be configured. This value is not stored in Terraform plan or state artifacts. Pair with `value_wo_version` to trigger secret value updates.

value_wo_version.description: Non-empty, non-secret version identifier for `value_wo`. Required when `value_wo` is configured. Change this value when the write-only secret value changes, for example by using an external secret manager version ID.

block.description:
A Cluster Secret is an encrypted key-value pair that can be accessed by agents within a cluster.
Secrets are encrypted and can only be accessed by agents that match the access policy.

**Note:** Secret values are write-only in the Buildkite API and cannot be retrieved after they are set.
Exactly one of value or value_wo must be configured. The value attribute is stored in
Terraform state so Terraform can detect changes. Use value_wo with value_wo_version
to pass a secret value without storing it in Terraform plan or state artifacts.

allowed_api_ip_addresses.description:
A list of IP addresses in CIDR format that are allowed to access the Buildkite API.If not set, all IP addresses are allowed (the same as setting 0.0.0.0/0).

-> The "Allowed API IP Addresses" feature must be enabled on your organization in order to manage the `allowed_api_ip_addresses` attribute.

enforce_2fa.description: Sets whether the organization requires two-factor authentication for all members.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the organization.

block.description:
This resource allows you to manage the settings for an organization.

The user of your API token must be an organization administrator to manage organization settings.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the organization banner.

uuid.description: The UUID of the organization banner.

block.description:
This resource allows you to create and manage banners for specific organizations, displayed to all members at the top of each page in Buildkite's UI.

More information on organization/system banners can be found in the [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/team-management/system-banners).

action.description: The action defined between source and target resources.

description.description: The description of the organization rule.

effect.description: Whether this organization rule allows or denies the action to take place between source and target resources.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the organization rule.

source_type.description: The source resource type that this organization rule allows or denies to invoke its defined action.

source_uuid.description: The UUID of the resource that this organization rule allows or denies invocating its defined action.

target_type.description: The target resource type that this organization rule allows or denies the source to respective action.

target_uuid.description: The UUID of the target resource that this organization rule allows or denies invocation its respective action.

uuid.description: The UUID of the organization rule.

value.description: The JSON document that this organization rule implements.

block.description:
An Organization Rule allows specifying explicit rules between two Buildkite resources and the desired effect/action.

More information on organization rules can be found in the [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/rules).

allow_rebuilds.description: Whether rebuilds are allowed for this pipeline.

archived.description: Whether to archive this pipeline. Archived pipelines are hidden from most views and cannot run new builds.

badge_url.description: The badge URL showing build state.

branch_configuration.description: Configure the pipeline to only build on this branch conditional.

cancel_intermediate_builds.description: Whether to cancel builds when a new commit is pushed to a matching branch.

cancel_intermediate_builds_branch_filter.description: Filter the `cancel_intermediate_builds` setting based on this branch condition.

cluster_id.description: Attach this pipeline to the given cluster GraphQL ID.

cluster_name.description: The name of the cluster the pipeline is (optionally) attached to.

color.description: A color hex code to represent this pipeline.

default_team_id.description: The GraphQL ID of a team to initially assign to the pipeline. This is required by the Buildkite API when creating a new pipeline. The team assigned here will be given 'Manage Build and Read' access. Further team associations can be managed with the `buildkite_pipeline_team` resource after the pipeline is created.

default_timeout_in_minutes.description: Set pipeline wide timeout for command steps.

description.description: Description for the pipeline. Can include emoji 🙌.

emoji.description: An emoji that represents this pipeline.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline.

maximum_timeout_in_minutes.description: Set pipeline wide maximum timeout for command steps.

pipeline_template_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline template applied to this pipeline.

build_branches.description: Whether to create builds when branches are pushed.

build_check_run_completed.description: Whether to create a build when a GitHub check run completes. Useful for chaining CI workflows by triggering a Buildkite pipeline after another CI system finishes.

build_create_event.description: Whether to create a build when a branch or tag is created on GitHub.

build_deployment_status_created.description: Whether to create a build when a GitHub deployment status is created.

build_issue_comment_created.description: Whether to create builds when an issue comment is created on a pull request.

build_merge_group_checks_requested.description: Whether to create merge queue builds for a merge queue enabled GitHub repository with required status checks

build_pull_request_base_branch_changed.description: Whether to create builds for pull requests when its base branch changes.

build_pull_request_converted_to_draft.description: Whether to create a build when a pull request is converted to a draft.

build_pull_request_forks.description: Whether to create builds for pull requests from third-party forks.

build_pull_request_labels_changed.description: Whether to create builds for pull requests when labels are added or removed.

build_pull_request_merge_commits.description: Whether to build the test merge commit (the merged result of a pull request with its base branch).

build_pull_request_ready_for_review.description: Whether to create a build when a pull request changes to "Ready for review".

build_pull_request_review_dismissed.description: Whether to create a build when a pull request review is dismissed.

build_pull_request_review_requested.description: Whether to create a build when a review is requested on a pull request.

build_pull_request_review_submitted.description: Whether to create a build when a pull request review is submitted.

build_pull_requests.description: Whether to create builds for commits that are part of a pull request.

build_release_created.description: Whether to create a build when a GitHub release is created (including drafts).

build_release_published.description: Whether to create a build when a GitHub release is published.

build_release_released.description: Whether to create a build when a GitHub release is published as final (excludes pre-releases and drafts).

build_tags.description: Whether to create builds when tags are pushed.

cancel_deleted_branch_builds.description: Automatically cancel running builds for a branch if the branch is deleted.

cancel_when_merge_group_destroyed.description: Whether to cancel any running builds belonging to a removed merge group.

filter_condition.description: The condition to evaluate when deciding if a build should run. This is only valid when `trigger_mode` is `code`. More details available in [the documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/conditionals).

filter_enabled.description: Whether to filter builds to only run when the condition in `filter_condition` is true.

ignore_default_branch_pull_requests.description: Whether to prevent caching pull requests with the source branch matching the default branch.

issue_comment_command_word.description: The command word used to trigger builds from issue comments (e.g. "/bk"). Only comments starting with or containing this word will trigger builds. Defaults to "/bk".

issue_comment_match_mode.description: The match mode for the issue comment command word. Valid values are "exact" and "contains". Defaults to "exact".

prefix_pull_request_fork_branch_names.description: Prefix branch names for third-party fork builds to ensure they don't trigger branch conditions. For example, the main branch from some-user will become some-user:main.

publish_blocked_as_pending.description: The status to use for blocked builds. Pending can be used with [required status checks](https://help.github.com/en/articles/enabling-required-status-checks) to prevent merging pull requests with blocked builds.

publish_commit_status.description: Whether to update the status of commits in Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitLab.

publish_commit_status_per_step.description: Whether to create a separate status for each job in a build, allowing you to see the status of each job directly in Bitbucket or GitHub.

pull_request_branch_filter_configuration.description: Filter pull requests builds by the branch filter.

separate_pull_request_statuses.description: Whether to create a separate status for pull request builds, allowing you to require a passing pull request build in your [required status checks](https://help.github.com/en/articles/enabling-required-status-checks) in GitHub.

skip_builds_for_existing_commits.description: Whether to skip creating a new build if an existing build for the commit and branch already exists. This option is only valid if the pipeline uses a GitHub repository.

skip_pull_request_builds_for_existing_co.description: Whether to skip creating a new build for a pull request if an existing build for the commit and branch already exists.

trigger_mode.description:
What type of event to trigger builds on. Must be one of:
	- `code` will create builds when code is pushed to GitHub.
	- `deployment` will create builds when a deployment is created in GitHub.
	- `fork` will create builds when the GitHub repository is forked.
	- `none` will not create any builds based on GitHub activity.

	-> `trigger_mode` is only valid if the pipeline uses a GitHub repository.
	-> If not set, the default value is `code` and other provider settings defaults are applied.

use_merge_group_base_commit_for_git_diff.description: When enabled, agents performing a git diff to determine steps to upload based on [`if_changed`](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/configure/step-types/command-step#agent-applied-attributes)comparisons will use the base commit that points to the previous merge group rather than the base branch

use_step_key_as_commit_status.description: Whether to use step keys as commit status names for per-step commit statuses. Requires `publish_commit_status` and `publish_commit_status_per_step` to also be enabled. Defaults to false.

provider_settings.description: Control settings depending on the VCS provider used in `repository`.

repository.description: URL to the repository this pipeline is configured for.

skip_intermediate_builds.description: Whether to skip queued builds if a new commit is pushed to a matching branch.

skip_intermediate_builds_branch_filter.description: Filter the `skip_intermediate_builds` setting based on this branch condition.

slug.description: A custom identifier for the pipeline. If provided, this slug will be used as the pipeline's URL path instead of automatically converting the pipeline name. If not provided, the slug will be [derived](https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/graphql/cookbooks/pipelines#create-a-pipeline-deriving-a-pipeline-slug-from-the-pipelines-name) from the pipeline `name`.

steps.description: The YAML steps to configure for the pipeline. Can also accept the `steps` attribute from the [`buildkite_signed_pipeline_steps`](/docs/data-sources/signed_pipeline_steps) data source to enable a signed pipeline. Defaults to `buildkite-agent pipeline upload`.

tags.description: Tags to attribute to the pipeline. Useful for searching by in the UI.

visibility.description: The visibility of the pipeline. Can be `PUBLIC` or `PRIVATE`. Only use `PUBLIC` visibility for pipelines without sensitive information. Defaults to `PRIVATE`.

webhook_url.description: The webhook URL used to trigger builds from VCS providers.

block.description:
This resource allows you to create and manage pipelines for repositories.

More information on pipelines can be found in the [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines).

-> **Note:** When creating a new pipeline, the Buildkite API requires at least one team to be associated with it. You must use the 'default_team_id' attribute to specify this initial team. The 'buildkite_pipeline_team' resource can then be used to manage team access for existing pipelines.

branch.description: The branch that the schedule should run on.

commit.description: The commit that the schedule should run on.

cronline.description: The cronline that describes when the schedule should run. See[here](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/scheduled-builds#schedule-intervals) for supported syntax.

enabled.description: Whether the schedule is enabled or not.

env.description: The environment variables that scheduled builds should use. An empty map (`{}`) is equivalent to omitting this attribute at the API level.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the schedule.

label.description: A label to describe the schedule.

message.description: The message the builds show for builds created by this schedule.

pipeline_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline that this schedule belongs to.

block.description:
A pipeline schedule is a schedule that triggers a pipeline to run at a specific time.

You can find more information in the [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/scheduled-builds).

access_level.description: The access level for the team. Either `READ_ONLY`, `BUILD_AND_READ` or `MANAGE_BUILD_AND_READ`.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline-team relationship.

pipeline_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline.

team_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team.

uuid.description: The UUID of the pipeline-team relationship.

block.description: Manage team access to a pipeline.

available.description: If the pipeline template is available for assignment by non admin users.

configuration.description: The YAML step configuration for the pipeline template.

description.description: A description for the pipeline template.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline template.

name.description: The name of the pipeline template.

uuid.description: The UUID of the pipeline template.

block.description:
This resource allows for standardized step configurations that can be used within various pipelines of an organization.

More information on pipeline templates can be found in the [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/templates).

id.description: The ID of the webhook.

pipeline_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the pipeline.

repository.description: The repository URL the webhook is configured for. The webhook will be replaced when this value changes.

webhook_url.description: The Buildkite webhook URL that receives events from the repository.

block.description:
This resource manages a webhook for a Buildkite pipeline's source repository.

The webhook enables automatic build triggering when changes are pushed to the repository.
Only one webhook can exist per pipeline - if a webhook already exists, it will be adopted into state.

Only supported for GitHub and GitHub Enterprise repositories connected via a
[GitHub App](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/source-control/github#connect-your-buildkite-account-to-github-using-the-github-app).

~> The `repository` attribute must match the pipeline's configured repository URL.
Use `repository = buildkite_pipeline.<name>.repository` to keep them in sync.

allowed_ip_addresses.description: Space-delimited list of IP addresses (in CIDR notation) allowed to invoke this portal. If not specified, all IP addresses are allowed.

created_at.description: The time when the portal was created.

created_by.description: Information about the user who created the portal.

description.description: A description of the portal.

query.description: The GraphQL query that the portal executes.

slug.description: The slug of the portal. Used in the portal's URL path.

token.description: The token used to invoke the portal. Only returned on creation.

user_invokable.description: Whether users can invoke the portal. Defaults to false.

block.description:
This resource allows you to manage portals in Buildkite. Portals allow you to expose GraphQL queries
that can be invoked via a REST API endpoint. Find out more information in our
[documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/portals).

color.description: A color representation of the registry. Accepts hex codes, eg #BADA55.

description.description:
This is a description for the registry, this may describe the usage for it, the region, or something else
which would help identify the registry's purpose.

ecosystem.description: The ecosystem of the registry. This value cannot be changed after creation.

emoji.description:
An emoji to use with the registry, this can either be set using :buildkite: notation, or with the
emoji itself, such as 🚀.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the registry.

name.description: The name of the registry. Can only contain numbers and letters, no spaces or special characters.

oidc_policy.description: The registry's OIDC policy, in YAML format.

public.description: Whether the registry is publicly accessible.

team_ids.description: The team UUIDs that have access to the registry. At least one team must be specified. This value cannot be changed after creation.

block.description:
This resource allows you to create and manage a Buildkite Registry.
Find out more information in our [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/package-registries).

default_member_role.description: The default role for new members of the team. This can be either `MEMBER` or `MAINTAINER`.

default_team.description: Whether this is the default team for the organization.

description.description: A description for the team. This is displayed in the Buildkite UI.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team.

members_can_create_pipelines.description: Whether members of the team can create Pipelines.

members_can_create_registries.description: Whether members of the team can create registries.

members_can_create_suites.description: Whether members of the team can create test suites.

members_can_destroy_packages.description: Whether members of the team can destroy packages.

members_can_destroy_registries.description: Whether members of the team can destroy registries.

privacy.description: The privacy setting for the team. This can be either `VISIBLE` or `SECRET`.

slug.description: The generated slug for the team.

block.description: A Team is a group of users that can be given permissions for using Pipelines.This feature is only available to Business and Enterprise customers.  You can find out more about Teams in the Buildkite [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/team-management/permissions).

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team membership.

role.description: The role for the user. Either `MEMBER` or `MAINTAINER`.

team_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team.

user_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the user.

uuid.description: The UUID of the team membership.

block.description: A team member resource allows for the management of team membership for existing organization users.

api_token.description: The API token to use to send test run data to the API.

default_branch.description: The default branch for the repository this test suite is for.

emoji.description: The emoji associated with this test suite, eg :buildkite:

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the test suite.

name.description: The name to give the test suite.

slug.description: The generated slug of the test suite.

team_owner_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team to mark as the owner/admin of the test suite.

uuid.description: The UUID of the test suite.

block.description: A test suite is a collection of tests. A run is to a suite what a build is to a Pipeline.Use this resource to manage [Test Suites](https://buildkite.com/docs/test-analytics) on Buildkite.

access_level.description: The access level the team has on the test suite. Either `READ_ONLY` or `MANAGE_AND_READ`.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the test suite-team relationship.

team_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the team.

test_suite_id.description: The GraphQL ID of the test suite.

uuid.description: The UUID of the test suite-team relationship.

block.description: Manage team access to a test suite.

description.description: The description of the cluster.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster.

actor_email.description: The email of the actor (only for users).

actor_slug.description: The slug of the actor (only for teams).

actor_type.description: The type of the actor (user or team).

actor_uuid.description: The UUID of the actor (user or team).

permission_uuid.description: The UUID of the maintainer permission.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers (users and teams) for this cluster.

name.description: The name of the cluster to retrieve.

block.description: Use this data source to retrieve a cluster by name. You can find out more about clusters in the Buildkite [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/clusters/overview).

description.description: The description of the default queue.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the default queue.

key.description: The key of the default queue.

uuid.description: The UUID of the default queue.

default_queue.description: The default queue for the cluster.

description.description: The description of the cluster.

id.description: The GraphQL ID of the cluster.

actor_email.description: The email of the actor (only for users).

actor_slug.description: The slug of the actor (only for teams).

actor_type.description: The type of the actor (user or team).

actor_uuid.description: The UUID of the actor (user or team).

permission_uuid.description: The UUID of the maintainer permission.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers (users and teams) for this cluster.

block.description:
Use this data source to retrieve clusters of an organization. You can find out more about clusters in the Buildkite
[documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/v3/clusters).

id.description: Fixed value: `https://api.buildkite.com/v2/meta`.

webhook_ips.description: List of IPs in CIDR format.

block.description:
Use this data source to look up the source IP addresses that Buildkite may use to send external requests,
including webhooks and API calls to source control systems (like GitHub Enterprise Server and BitBucket Server).

More info in the Buildkite [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/rest-api/meta).

jwks.description:
The JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) to use for signing.
All double-quotes in the JSON object must be escaped `\"`.
If `jwks_key_id` is not specified, and the set contains exactly one key, that key will
be used.

~> **Security Notice** The secret key in the `jwks` attribute will be stored
*unencrypted* in your Terraform state file. This attribute is designed for
users that have systems to to securely manage their state files. If you wish
to avoid this, use the `jwks_file` attribute instead.

jwks_file.description:
The path to a file containing the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) to use for
signing. Users will have to ensure that the JWKS file is present on systems
running Terraform. If `jwks` is specified, this will be ignored and the
JWKS will be parsed from that value instead. If `jwks_key_id` is not specified, and the
set contains exactly one key, that key will be used.

~> **Security Notice** The secret key referenced in the `jwks_file` attribute is
expected to be stored *unencrypted* as a file on the system running
Terraform. You are responsible for securing it on this system while
Terraform is running, and cleaning it up after it has finished running.

jwks_key_id.description:
The ID of the key in the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) to use for signing.
If this is not specified, and the key set contains exactly one key, that key
will be used.

repository.description: The repository that will be checked out in a build of the pipeline.

steps.description: The signed steps in YAML format.

unsigned_steps.description: The steps to sign in YAML format.

block.description:
Use this data source to sign pipeline steps with a JWKS key. You will need to have
the corresponding verification key present on the agents that run this the steps in
this pipeline. You can then use these steps in a `buildkite_pipeline` resource.

See [RFC 7517](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7517) for more information
about the JWKS format.

See the Buildkite [documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/v3/signed_pipelines)
for more info about signed pipelines.

Note that the PS512 and ES512 signature algorithms are nondeterministic and
will result in the signature changing on each run. Use EdDSA to avoid drift.
